claims.text: Favorable electron-phonon interactions enable coherent electron pairing and superconductivity in the HEA.
High atomic disorder initially suppresses the electron-phonon interactions needed for superconductivity.
Moderate annealing partially reduces chemical disorder.
Annealing-induced reduction of chemical disorder enhances electron-phonon interactions and raises the superconducting transition temperature.
The starting as-cast HEA has significant atomic-scale disorder and inhomogeneity.
Annealing at approximately 700°C for several hours in an inert atmosphere can partially relieve atomic disorder while retaining the overall high-entropy composition.
The annealed sample will have reduced atomic disorder and improved local chemical homogeneity.
Reduced disorder and improved local chemical homogeneity produce a more coherent lattice.
A more coherent lattice supports enhanced electron-phonon coupling.
Atomic-scale randomness in the as-cast state increases electron scattering.
Increased electron scattering weakens the electron-phonon coupling necessary for Cooper-pair formation.
Annealing lowers electron-scattering rates by reducing disorder.
Lower scattering rates enhance the pairing interaction and promote superconductivity at a higher transition temperature.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will exhibit a higher superconducting transition temperature.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the annealed alloy will exhibit a sharper superconducting transition, zero electrical resistivity, and a stronger diamagnetic response below 10 K.
In the as-cast baseline, superconductivity is absent or significantly suppressed, with a lower transition temperature or broad and weak superconducting signatures.
The proposed relationship between reduced disorder and enhanced superconductivity should apply to HEAs with similar compositions and processing histories.
Extreme composition changes or substantially different thermal processing may fall outside the regime in which reduced disorder enhances superconductivity.
